stories.title: Mini brain organoids ‘reading’ Braille marks key step towards biohybrid computing
stories.description: A group of scientists have shown that brain organoids can pass on signals that correspond to Braille letters, an essential step towards developing the energy-efficient biohybrid computers of the future. The brain organoids, remotely connected to a sensor that recorded tactile signals from different Braille letters, produced signals that were different for each letter, allowing a decoder to distinguish between the different letters the organoids had been given. Although individual brain organoids provided accurately decodable signals 61% of the time, a team of three performed significantly better, producing an accurate signal 83% of the time. The team of three was also better at distinguishing the signals from artificial noise than the decoder working directly on the obscured signals, without the organoids’ involvement.

stories.title: Expansion of Bragg reflection width in elastomer-immobilized colloidal photonic crystals via binary monomer mixing
stories.description: This study aimed to demonstrate that the Bragg reflection width of elastomer-immobilized, nonclose-packed colloidal photonic crystal films can be expanded using a mixture of two elastomer precursors. The water present inside the gel-immobilized colloidal photonic crystal films was replaced with a binary solution of 4-hydroxybutyl acrylate (4HBA) and 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (2HEMA) at different 2HEMA mass fractions (w2H). The samples were subsequently photopolymerized under ultraviolet light irradiation. For the elastomer-immobilized, nonclose-packed colloidal photonic crystal film exclusively prepared using 4HBA, the full width at half maximum of the Bragg reflection peak was 19 nm; this value increased to 186 nm when the film was prepared at w2H = 0.3. This expansion is attributed to the swelling–shrinkage behavior of the polymer during slow photopolymerization induced by the addition of 2HEMA. This simple expansion method is expected to advance the practical applications of these crystals as structural color materials, wide-band optical filters, and tunable photonic crystals. A simple method for expanding the Bragg reflection width of elastomer-immobilized, nonclose-packed colloidal photonic crystal films using a mixture of two types of elastomer precursors was proposed. For the elastomer-immobilized, nonclose-packed colloidal photonic crystal film exclusively prepared using 4-hydroxybutyl acrylate (4HBA), the full width at half maximum of the Bragg reflection peak was 19 nm; this value increased to 186 nm by the addition of 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (2HEMA). This expansion method is expected to advance the practical applications of these crystals as structural color materials and wide-band optical filters.
